topic: Locating points on the coordinate plane
summary: The deck introduces the coordinate plane through an airfield metaphor: the x- and y-axes, ordered pairs (x, y), the four quadrants and negative coordinates, ending with practice tasks for guiding aircraft. An optional extension introduces the distance formula.

concepts.name: Axes and origin
concepts.description: The x-axis runs left to right, the y-axis bottom to top, and they cross at the origin (0, 0).

concepts.name: Ordered pairs
concepts.description: (x, y): move along x first (right is positive), then along y (up is positive).

concepts.name: Quadrants
concepts.description: The axes split the plane into four quadrants identified by the signs of x and y; points on an axis are in no quadrant.

concepts.name: Negative coordinates
concepts.description: A negative sign means left (for x) or down (for y); the number is the distance.

concepts.name: Distance between points (extension)
concepts.description: The distance formula, offered as optional extension material.

prerequisites.text: Counting on a number line, including negative numbers.

objectives.text: Locate and plot a point from an ordered pair (x, y), moving along x first and then y.
Identify the quadrant of a point from the signs of its coordinates.
Interpret negative coordinates as movement to the left or downward.
Compare and order points by their x-coordinates.

examples.text: (−4, −3) means 4 left, then 3 down, and lies in Quadrant III.

questions.prompt: Which way do you move first for the point (3, −2)?

interactions.description: Guide an aircraft to a runway or hangar given as an ordered pair.
Sort points into the quadrant they belong to.
Line aircraft up from left to right by x-coordinate.
